main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking devil curry given that the smell bothers A (calls), B (room/clothes) and C (laundry), and what timing or notice arrangement would settle it.

A-B.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling food and accepted the after-7 timing (T5, T7); B said timing doesn't help but accepted advance notice (T8, T12, T16). They never addressed each other, but both ended up accepting D's arrangement.

A-C.evidence: A asked for after 7 or weekends (T5); C said evenings don't help (T9) and asked D to avoid Mon/Wed/Fri (T23). Neither addressed the other. Both accepted D's final accommodations.

A-D.evidence: D initially said 'I hear you' (T4), then agreed to cook after 7 (T6) and A thanked D (T7). D later added notice and avoiding C's laundry days (T13, T27), so the final arrangement satisfies A's request.

B-C.evidence: C said 'Same for me' (T9), backing B's point that after 7 doesn't help. They later needed different fixes: B accepted notice (T16), C asked for no cooking on laundry days (T23).

B-D.evidence: B said after 7 doesn't help (T8) and asked for notice (T12). D agreed to notify (T13) and B said 'that works for me' (T16).

C-D.evidence: C rejected the notice and the laundry-moving help (T14, T18, T21). D then offered to avoid Mon/Wed/Fri (T22), C asked for that (T23) and D agreed (T27).
